fact: MEDDIC was created in 1996 inside PTC (Parametric Technology Corporation) by Dick Dunkel, working under SVP John McMahon alongside teammate Jack Napoli, to address sales attrition by studying what drove won, lost and slipped deals.

Dick Dunkel and Jack Napoli created the six-letter framework inside PTC in 1996 by reverse-engineering deals PTC won versus lost; Napoli's PTC alumni network spread it to other enterprise software companies.
MEDDIC was 'conceived in the 1990s by two sales experts, Dick Dunkel and Jack Napoli' (no PTC or McMahon mention in this source).
Dick Dunkel is described as 'the creator of MEDDIC'; he worked at Xerox, then PTC, and 'PTC would be where he came up with the six elements of MEDDIC.'
John McMahon was CRO at five public enterprise software companies (PTC, GeoTel, Ariba, BladeLogic, BMC); 'PTC is where the MEDDIC qualification framework originated.'

McMahon's career per MongoDB board announcement (Oct 2016): PTC (revenue grew $1M to $1.1B in nine years), GeoTel (acquired by Cisco for $2B), Ariba, BladeLogic (COO, IPO), BMC (responsible for $1.4B annual revenue).

MEDDPICC stands for Metrics, Economic Buyer, Decision Criteria, Decision Process, Paper Process, Identify Pain, Champion, Competition. MEDDIC evolved into MEDDPICC with the addition of Paper Process and Competition.

MEDDPICC adds Paper Process (legal, procurement and security steps after a verbal yes) and Competition (every alternative, including doing nothing) to MEDDIC; the eight-letter version was formalised in the 2010s by Andy Whyte / MEDDICC organization.

Force Management was founded in 2002 by Grant Wilson (CEO) and John Kaplan (President), headquartered in Charlotte, NC. Its proprietary curriculum includes Command of the Message, Command of the Sale, Command of the Plan, Command of the Talent, Value Negotiation and MEDDICC. TZP Group led a recapitalization in July 2021.
Force Management co-founder John Kaplan was previously SVP of International Sales Operations at PTC (and nine years at Xerox).

Force Management delivers MEDDICC training as instructor-led programs plus online learning and certification on its Ascender platform, with Opportunity Qualifiers and Opportunity Coaching Guides. Customer testimonial (Intercom): 'We implemented Force Management's Command of the Message and MEDDPICC.'

Force Management defines Command of the Message as 'being audible-ready to define your solutions to customer problems' in a differentiated way; its terms include Before Scenario, Value Drivers, Required Capabilities, Positive Business Outcomes, metrics, customer proof points, and the Value Messaging Framework.

Command of the Message Value Framework components: Before Scenarios, Negative Consequences, After Scenarios, Positive Business Outcomes, Required Capabilities, Metrics, How We Do It, How We Do It Better, Proof Points, plus discovery and trap-setting questions.

Third-party summary of the value framework: Before Scenario, Negative Consequences, Positive Business Outcomes, Required Capabilities, Metrics, Differentiators, Proof Points, discovery/trap-setting questions. It also says Force Management created and licenses Command of the Message, teaches MEDDICC, and that Kaplan was on the PTC sales team where MEDDIC emerged.

An alternate summary names the concepts Current State, Negative Consequences, Future State, Positive Business Outcomes, Value Drivers, Required Capabilities, Metrics, Differentiators, Proof Points and The Mantra.
Force Management case study references its Value Framework, outlining 'positive business outcomes' and 'the required capabilities to achieve them.'

The Qualified Sales Leader: Proven Lessons from a Five Time CRO by John McMahon, published May 5, 2021 (self-published); aimed at enterprise software sales leaders and reps; reviewers call it a definitive text on MEDDPICC.
The Qualified Sales Leader was published in 2021; McMahon is described as a former CRO at five public enterprise software companies.
McMahon co-hosts the Revenue Builders podcast with John Kaplan of Force Management and has served on the boards of Snowflake and MongoDB.
